_readme: Copy library for the seven lifecycle emails. PostHog holds only whichever variant is currently live on each step - this file is the source of truth and its git history is the record of every decision the weekly loop has made. build_email.py turns an entry here into the exact payload workflows-patch-action-email expects; decide.py chooses which entry that should be; optimise.md is the runbook the scheduled job follows. Exactly one variant per step is 'champion' and at most one is 'testing'; two can never be live at once because PostHog has no split node, which is why the test is sequential - see the top of decide.py for what that costs.

_angles.utility: No persuasion. Tells them the one thing to do and gets out of the way.
_angles.question: Subject is a real question. Questions are the highest-opening subject format measured (~46%), and a reply is the cleanest engagement signal there is.
_angles.specific: Concrete number or outcome in the subject. Specific curiosity beats vague teasing by ~26%; vague teasing also wins opens and loses clicks.
_angles.empathy: Names the awkwardness out loud. Beats urgency on win-back - 'did we lose you' outperforms 'final notice'.
_angles.confession: Leads with something that went wrong on our side. The register that earned 29% replies on the old campaign.
_angles.peer: Speaks in another user's voice rather than the company's. Unlocks accounts that company-voice email cannot.
_angles.permission: Offers to stop emailing. Counter-intuitively strong on dormant lists and cleans the list either way.
